paragraphs: In the morning of 7 October 2023, during the Jewish holidays of Simchat Torah and Shemini Atzeret on Shabbat, Hamas announced the start of "Operation Al-Aqsa Flood", firing between 3,000 and 5,000 rockets from the Gaza Strip into Israel within a span of 20 minutes. Simultaneously, around 3,000 Hamas militants infiltrated Israel from Gaza using trucks, motorcycles, bulldozers, speedboats, and paragliders. They took over checkpoints at Kerem Shalom and Erez, and created openings in the border fence in five other places.

Militants massacred civilians in several kibbutzim, where they took hostages and set fire to homes. In a massacre at an outdoor music festival "nova" near Re'im, at least 325 people were killed, with more injured or taken hostage. In total, 251 people, mostly civilians, were taken hostage, including children, elderly people, and soldiers. Hamas militants also engaged in mutilation, torture, and sexual and gender-based violence.

known_discrepancy: Nova festival toll: the user's text says 'at least 325'. No reputable source opened here uses 325. Israeli authorities' figure is 'at least 364' killed at the festival (Times of Israel; UN COI A/HRC/56/CRP.3: 379 killed at the site, near kibbutz Re'im or adjacent, of whom at least 364 were festival attendees); an IDF probe reported by Ynet counts 378 killed in and around the site. 'At least 325' is true as a lower bound but is outdated; the text is kept as the user wrote it. Other places where the user's text differs from sourced figures: (1) '3,000 to 5,000 rockets within 20 minutes': Hamas claimed over 5,000 (ToI liveblog), the IDF counted 2,200 by 10:26 and later 'at least 5,000' on 7 October, a later Israeli analysis says about 3,700; no opened source gives the 20-minute window. (2) 'around 3,000 Hamas militants': the UN COI says Hamas planned 3,000 plus 1,500 in support; Israeli analyses put those who crossed at about 5,600-6,000 including civilians. (3) 'openings in the fence in five other places': the UN COI says at least 29 locations and a later Israeli analysis says 119 spots. (4) 'took over checkpoints at Kerem Shalom and Erez': the UN COI lists the Kerem Shalom and Erez Crossing positions among eight military bases/outposts attacked, but no opened source says they were 'taken over'. (5) 'speedboats': sources say rubber boats / infiltration by sea. (6) 'mutilation, torture': the UN SRSG-SVC report found widespread mutilation of bodies and credible information of sexualized torture of hostages, but says specific genital-mutilation claims could not be verified.
